title: Benchmark design: orch-ON vs orch-OFF token cost (headless arms, judge-subtree shape)
summary: Analytic to measure the net token effect of orchestrator context/knowledge vs a bare agent, on the SAME fixed solution spec. Design (user-decided 2026-06-08): mirror the self-learning judge subtree — problem P → arm A (orch-ON) + arm B (orch-OFF) → analysis node J (blocked_by A,B) that records a benchmark verdict into get_learnings(). ARMS = separate HEADLESS `claude -p` processes, each with its own --mcp-config (A loads orchestrator-graph; B loads NONE so it truly has no orch tools — clean enforcement, no runtime nudge needed) and its own transcript (clean per-arm token attribution; avoids the same-session-collapse problem where Agent-tool subagents log into the parent transcript). MEASUREMENT: per-arm transcript summed via readUsage-style accounting; SUBTRACT mcp__orchestrator-graph__* tool_use/tool_result tokens → report gross / net / plumbing. Scope: TWO problems (one context-RICH where the graph has relevant learnings so A can actually inherit context — fair test; one GREENFIELD self-contained — biases against orch, measures pure plumbing) × 2 arms × 3 trials = 12 runs; aggregate mean+stdev. Output: graph subtree (structure) + J summary (headline) + verdict in learnings (durable) + bench/report.{md,json} (detail). Runtime-nudge guard (ORCH_CONTROL) is the FALLBACK only if headless proves infeasible. Key risk spiked first: does headless claude -p --mcp-config run here + where is its transcript.
